description: Heavy-stutter / hard-block reconstruction test corpus. Each script simulates the verbatim ASR output (Whisper or device ASR) that a speaker with hard silent blocks would produce. Ground-truth 'intended' is what the speaker meant to say. Reconstruction quality is scored against intended, not against disfluent.
design_notes: Distinct from tests/stutter_pipeline/test_cases.json (which covers audible disfluencies). This corpus targets the silent-block / hard-block case George specifically needs to clear before foundation outreach. Patterns drawn from: SEP-28k block-labeled clips (Apple 2021), FluencyBank Timestamped (Bayerl 2024), Howell 2004 disfluency taxonomy, plus George's lived speech-block phenomenology.
block_token_convention: [BLOCK] = silent freeze that an attentive ASR would emit as nothing or as a short hallucinated word. [BLOCK-LONG] = >2 second silent freeze. '...' = audible pause, breath. '--' = mid-word abandonment. Phantom words from Whisper hallucinating during silence are spelled out inline (e.g. 'so so the'). Transcripts are in lowercase and use no end punctuation, mirroring Whisper raw output style.

cases.intended: I want to present the proposal on Tuesday
cases.disfluent: i want to [BLOCK] [BLOCK] present the proposal on tuesday
cases.notes: Two silent freezes before the hard /p/ content word. Whisper typically emits nothing during the freeze. Lavrentiy must reassemble across the gap.

cases.type: Whisper hallucinated word during silent block
cases.disfluent: can you so so so call the doctor
cases.notes: Classic Whisper failure mode: silence triggers hallucination of high-frequency token ('so'). Lavrentiy must recognize 'so so so' as filler not intent.

cases.type: long silent block with audible breath and restart
cases.intended: My biggest concern is the deadline
cases.disfluent: my biggest [BLOCK-LONG] uhh my my biggest concern is the deadline
cases.notes: Speaker abandons mid-phrase, freezes, breathes, restarts the same phrase. False-start detection plus block recovery.

cases.intended: I think we should reschedule the meeting
cases.disfluent: i think we sh-- we should res-- we should reschedule the meeting
cases.notes: Two mid-word abandonments before the blocked word completes. Lavrentiy must drop the abandoned fragments without losing the eventual completion.

cases.disfluent: i agree with i mean i i disagree with the recommendation
cases.notes: Speaker says opposite-meaning placeholder to escape the block then corrects. ALWAYS RESTATE rule must respect the correction, not the placeholder.

cases.intended: The cost is forty thousand dollars
cases.disfluent: the cost is uh fourteen actually forty thousand dollars
cases.notes: Number-substitution self-correction. Reconstruction must take 'forty' over 'fourteen' and drop both the filler and the original wrong number.

cases.type: multiple blocks in single utterance under phone stress
cases.intended: Hi this is George I am calling about the appointment on Thursday
cases.disfluent: hi this is [BLOCK] g g george i am [BLOCK] calling about the the appointment on [BLOCK] thursday
cases.notes: Three hard blocks plus part-word repetition on the proper noun. Tests proper-noun preservation through a block.

cases.intended: I need to talk to my manager about the raise
cases.disfluent: i need to uhm uh well you know like uhm talk to my manager about the the raise
cases.notes: Heavy filler cluster used as a postponement strategy before the feared content word ('talk' triggers block). Different mechanism than h07's overt block but functionally equivalent.

cases.type: email dictation with blocks and self-correction
cases.intended: Please send the revised contract before close of business Friday
cases.disfluent: please uhh please please send the the [BLOCK] revised contract uh before close of of business friday
cases.notes: Casual office dictation, three repetition events plus one silent block before content word.

cases.intended: I met with Henderson at the Marriott yesterday
cases.disfluent: i met with [BLOCK] [BLOCK] henderson at the the m m marriott yesterday
cases.notes: Two blocks on first proper noun, part-word repetition on second. Tests proper-noun preservation under reconstruction (must NOT substitute generic placeholder).

cases.intended: Good morning everyone today I want to talk about the quarterly results
cases.disfluent: good [BLOCK-LONG] uhm good morning everyone uh today i i want to [BLOCK] talk about the the quarterly results
cases.notes: Long opening freeze, recovery, then second block on the verb. Common presentation-stress pattern.

cases.type: medical context with block on diagnostic term
cases.intended: I have been experiencing chest pain for about two weeks
cases.disfluent: i have been experiencing uhh ch-- ch-- [BLOCK] chest pain for about uh two weeks
cases.notes: Mid-word abandonment plus block on the medically-loaded word. Domain pack medical may engage.

cases.disfluent: want to uh g g grab dinner [BLOCK] tonight
cases.notes: Friend-tone test. Low-stress block pattern. Reconstruction must keep informal voice, not formalize.

cases.type: legal context with block on stakes-laden phrase
cases.intended: I do not consent to that condition
cases.disfluent: i do not [BLOCK] [BLOCK] consent to that uh that condition
cases.notes: Blocks on the most consequential phrase. Reconstruction must NOT soften 'do not consent' to something hedged.

cases.type: bilingual EN-RU with Russian filler postponing English block
cases.intended: Can you please pass me the salt
cases.disfluent: can you ну ну please p p [BLOCK] pass me the salt
cases.notes: Russian filler 'ну' used to postpone the English-onset block. George profile bilingual case.

cases.type: Whisper hallucinates 'the' during long silent block
cases.intended: I went to the conference last weekend
cases.disfluent: i went to the the the the conference last weekend
cases.notes: Whisper fills a 3-second silent block with repeated 'the' tokens. Lavrentiy must collapse, not preserve.

cases.intended: I think the new policy is unfair to junior staff
cases.disfluent: i think the new the the i i think the new policy is unfair to to junior staff
cases.notes: Speaker starts sentence, blocks, abandons, restarts identical sentence. Lavrentiy must recognize the abandonment-restart pattern and emit one clean sentence.

cases.intended: I need to call my therapist
cases.disfluent: i need to uh c c [BLOCK] reach out to my therapist
cases.notes: Speaker blocks on 'call', substitutes 'reach out to'. If covert profile flags 'call' as avoided, ALWAYS RESTATE should restore 'call'. If not, preserve 'reach out to'. Tests covert-avoidance logic.
